question: Why were so few large wild animals ever domesticated?
answer: Of the 148 big wild plant-eating mammals, only 14 were domesticated in ancient times, 13 of them in Eurasia. Diamond's 'Anna Karenina principle': a domestic animal needs everything to go right, from diet and growth to temper and breeding in captivity. Zebras bite and never let go; that one flaw is enough.
move: Success often needs everything to go right; failure needs one flaw.
simply: To be a farm animal you must pass a long exam: eat cheap food, grow fast, stay calm, breed in pens. Fail one question, like zebras with their bite, and you're out.
why: The same logic explains why most start-ups, recipes and plans fail: success needs every condition met, failure only one. Checking for the single deal-breaker saves effort.
source: Jared Diamond, Guns, Germs, and Steel, 1997
reference: Jared Diamond, Guns, Germs, and Steel (W. W. Norton, 1997), ch. 9
